title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 29 (Public Offer of Securities to Be in Dematerialised Form)

content.overview: Section 29 requires every company making a public offer, and such other class or classes of public companies as may be prescribed, to issue the securities only in dematerialised form under the Depositories Act, 1996 and regulations. Prescribed unlisted companies must facilitate demat holding and transfer.
content.glance: Public offers must be in demat form; prescribed classes of companies face the same rule.
content.study: A company making a public offer must issue securities only in dematerialised form under the Depositories Act, 1996. Other prescribed public companies must do the same. Prescribed unlisted companies must facilitate dematerialisation of existing securities and issue/transfer only in demat form.

sections.heading: Public Offer in Demat Form
sections.body: Every company making a public offer must issue securities only in dematerialised form under the Depositories Act.

sections.heading: Prescribed Classes
sections.body: Other prescribed public companies and unlisted companies may be brought under demat-only rules.
